/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2652 (49)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3886 (184)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1965 (-56)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1878 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1017 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market built on the positive momentum seen late yesterday, with sentiment improving across both basins and the BCI 182 5TC gaining $1,670 to close at $35,245. The C5 index increased by $0.555 to $14.50, while C3 jumped $1.690 to $35.505. In the Pacific, the market found better support as two C5 miners entered the market, alongside a couple of Japanese coal tenders and increased operator activity. Offers on C5 were heard in the upper $14s to start the day, with reports of one miner paying $14.25 and an operator linked to $14.40 on a Newcastlemax. There were also rumours of $14.60 being paid for a standard Capesize, reflecting the more positive tone as the day progressed. The Atlantic also continued to firm, led by improved activity from South Brazil and West Africa to China. Reports emerged of $35.50 being paid on C3, followed by $36.00 for end-November dates. These later dates continued to command a premium over index dates, currently 17–27 November. The North Atlantic was more mixed, however, with a weaker fixture putting some pressure on C8, which fell by $787 to $28,344.
PANAMAX
Continuing on the theme from previous days, the market remained under pressure, with sentiment continuing to weaken across both basins as the growing imbalance between available tonnage and cargo demand weighed on rates. The P5TC declined a further $507 to $17,686. In the Atlantic, trans-Atlantic activity remained limited, with market sources describing little fresh cargo entering the market and a growing tonnage list, particularly for prompt dates, allowing charterers to maintain the upper hand. Brokers highlighted that although some mineral requirements continued to provide opportunities for employment, rates remained under downward pressure, while grain demand offered little additional support. Sources stated that a wider bid-offer spread was emerging as owners were said to be showing greater resistance to revising numbers continually lower. Fronthaul sentiment remained weak, particularly from EC South America, as additional ballasting tonnage continued to compound the existing oversupply. The scrubber-fitted Golden Fellow (81,135 2020) EC South America 16 November was said to have been placed on subjects for a trans-Atlantic trip at $31,000, as was the Epic Harmony (82,546 2021) EC South America 10 November, both to Bunge. The scrubber-fitted Swift Hangzhou (79,343 2015) EC South America 14/16 November was reported to have fixed a trans-Atlantic grains stem at $25,000, although the charterer was not known. Bunge were reported to have fixed the Aristidis (82,177 2013) on a retroactive basis, having sailed Haldia on 19 October, for a fronthaul trip via EC South America at $17,250. In the Pacific, trading conditions were described as challenging, with charterers said to be continuing to dictate the pace of negotiations amid a lack of fresh momentum. North Pacific enquiry remained limited, while Indonesian business struggled to generate sufficient interest to provide any meaningful support to rates. EC Australian coal requirements continued to account for a reasonable proportion of activity, although the volume of available tonnage left owners facing increasing competition for employment. With little indication of an improvement in the underlying supply-demand balance, rates across the basin continued to drift lower. The Lagoon Trader (82,232 2024) open Kashima 5 November was reported to have been placed on subjects for a trip via EC Australia to Japan at $23,200, although no other details surfaced.
SUPRAMAX
A National holiday in Greece today meant an already quiet market lacked any meaningful direction as we pass midweek. The 11TC average was down $73 to $23,733 with most routes declining, and those that remained positive were by negligible amounts. The US Gulf continued to wane under a growing tonnage list with both grains and petcoke stems scarce and the resistance in East coast South America seems unable to cope with the competition from the Panamax market, with rates now easing. The Continent and Mediterranean markets are offering more resistance with fresh November demand evident, but rumoured trades elusive. Rates in Asia are flat with the market looking balanced in both the North and the South, whereas the Indian Ocean looks fragile with little in the way of forward cargoes appearing.
HANDYSIZE
After a subdued start to the week, the HS7TC was negative today by $58 to close at $18,304, driven mainly by the drop in the US Gulf. Sources claimed the area was extremely quiet today, with the St Lawrence/US east coast the only active area due to limited tonnage and the lack of vessels willing to ballast due to the Continent remaining firm, driven by clean cargoes to West Africa, scrap and increased Russian cargoes. The Mediterranean was more difficult to gauge with limited activity, whilst East coast South America remains very hot, despite the larger sizes seeing declines. In Asia the market remained mostly flat, although there was unconfirmed reports of a 38,000-dwt fixed at $19,250 from North China to South east Asia, and sources suggested there was ample tonnage now appearing, conversely there are many Chinese requirements which need deck cargo options.

Market Fundamentals
China Coal Demand
China’s coal consumption fell 2% year-on-year to 400 Mt in September, marking the fourth consecutive month of decline, as reported by McCloskey based on China Coal Transport and Distribution Association (CCTD) data. September demand from the power sector declined 1.1% to 230 Mt, while steel sector’s consumption decreased for the sixth consecutive month, down 5.0% to 60 Mt during the same period. In the year to September, demand stood 0.5% lower compared to the same period last year at 3.7 Bt.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape came under pressure during the afternoon, with Nov and Dec giving back early strength as prices weakened into the close. Nov opened at 36,500 before strengthening to 37,250, with heavy morning volume around 37,000. Prices then fell to 36,000 before finishing at 36,250. Dec opened at 37,250 and reached 37,400 before easing to 36,750, with notable late volume at the lower level. Q1 27 weakened from 28,700 to 28,350
